blocks.text: The Appeal of Acreage Living in Langley

parts.t: Langley acreages draw buyers looking for privacy, space, and a more rural lifestyle while still being close to the city. Areas like Campbell Valley, Salmon River, and Otter District are known for their large properties, hobby farms, and estate homes. Many acreage properties offer room for workshops, animals, gardens, or future development potential, making them a fit for families and hobby farmers.

Despite the quiet setting, most locations are still within a short drive of schools, shopping, and major commuter routes. Acreage properties in Langley tend to hold strong long-term value due to limited supply and consistent demand. If you're considering an acreage purchase, I can help you review zoning, land use potential, and recent comparable sales to find the right fit. Explore
On this site, an acreage is a home on 1 to 10 acres. Land over 10 acres is listed with
. Acreage listings come up in South Langley, Campbell Valley, Salmon River, Otter and around Aldergrove, and much of this rural land is in the Agricultural Land Reserve.

A 1 to 5 acre lot (1 to 4.99 acres) usually means a house with a big yard, room for a shop, gardens or a few animals, and more privacy than a town lot. Most run on a well and septic, so test water flow, water quality and the septic system before you remove subjects. Ask the Township of Langley what the zone allows for a second home, a shop or a suite, and check ALR status on the Agricultural Land Commission map.
At 5 to 10 acres there is room for barns, paddocks and an outdoor arena. Many buyers at this size keep horses, so see my
for homes on 5+ acres with barns and riding space. Ask whether barns and arenas were built with permits, how paddocks drain in winter, and whether any trail access crosses private land.
